The final battle of the {H_HUS_C}Hussite{##} Wars, fought on 30 May 1434 near the village of Lipany, east of {H_PRA_C}Prague{##}. Utraquists, a moderate faction of the Hussites, and their Catholic allies destroyed the radical Taborites and Orphans of {H_PROTHEGRE_C}Prokop the Great{##}, ending fifteen years of war and opening the way to {H_SIG_C}Sigismund's{##} late acceptance as King of {H_BOH_C}Bohemia{##}.

A kingdom in Central Europe and a powerful part of the {H_EMP_C}Empire{##}. Ruled during the early 15th century by the {H_HOUOFLUX_C}House of Luxembourg{##} from its capital at {H_PRA_C}Prague{##}. The king of Bohemia held one of the seven {H_ELE_C}electoral votes{##} in the Empire.
Bohemia

Brno was the principal city of the Margraviate of {H_MOR_C}Moravia{##}, set in southern Moravia. Granted royal town rights by King Wenceslaus I of Bohemia in 1243, it served as the seat of the Margraves of Moravia, including {H_JOBOFMOR_C}Jobst of Moravia{##}, who died here in 1411. Dominated by Špilberk Castle on the hill above, the city remained a German Catholic stronghold throughout the {H_HUS_C}Hussite{##} Wars, withstanding multiple sieges without ever falling.
Brno is also home to {H_ABG_C}Ashborne Games{##}!
Brno
14 May 1316 – 29 November 1378
Charles IV, King of Bohemia and Holy Roman Emperor, had a long and successful reign. The Empire he ruled from Prague expanded, and his subjects lived in peace and prosperity.
Emperor Charles IV

An agreement of 1436 between the Catholic Church and the moderate {H_HUS_C}Hussites{##}, granting partial recognition of Hussite religious practice and allowing {H_SIG_C}Sigismund{##} to be accepted at last as King of {H_BOH_C}Bohemia{##}.
Compacts Of Basel

A great council of the Catholic Church held in the Imperial city of Constance from 1414 to 1418, convened at {H_SIG_C}Sigismund's{##} urging. It ended the Western Schism by electing Pope Martin V in 1417 and condemned {H_JANHUS_C}Jan Hus{##} as a heretic in 1415, and had him burned at the stake.
Council Of Constance

Seven of the Empire's greatest rulers hold the privilege of electing the {H_KINOFROM_C}King of the Romans{##}. Established by the Golden Bull of 1356, the electoral college consists of the archbishops of Mainz, Cologne, and Trier, as well as four secular lords: the King of Bohemia, the Count Palatine of the Rhine, the Duke of Saxony, and the Margrave of Brandenburg.
Prince Elector

Holder of the highest title in the {H_EMP_C}Holy Roman Empire{##}, crowned by the Pope himself. After the death of {H_CHA4_C}Emperor Charles IV{##} in 1378, the throne stood vacant for fifty-five years, until {H_SIG_C}Sigismund{##} was finally crowned in 1433.
The Emperor

Founded by Charlemagne in 800 and restored by Otto the Great in 962, the Holy Roman Empire is the largest political entity in Central Europe. By the 15th century it stretches from the Low Countries (today's Netherlands and Belgium) in the west to the borders of Poland and Hungary in the east, and from the Baltic and North Seas down through the German lands, Austria, and Bohemia, with nominal authority over Northern Italy as well.

The Holy Roman Empire is ruled by the {H_EMPROR_C}Holy Roman Emperor{##}, the foremost among Catholic monarchs, crowned by the Pope himself. The throne has stood vacant since the death of {H_CHA4_C}Emperor Charles IV{##} in 1378, with the {H_KINOFROM_C}King of the Romans{##} holding power in the Emperor's stead.
The Holy Roman Empire
This is the final year of the demo, but your journey in Europa 1410 is just getting started.
Now that you have proven yourself a successful Master Smith in this town, why not try your hand at building a business empire in {H_KUT_C}Kuttenberg{##}, the silver crown of {H_BOH_C}Bohemia{##}.

You will get the chance to peek into Bohemia's turbulent history and understand the role of the {H_BATOFLIP_C}Hussite Wars{##} in shaping the history of the Catholic Church and the {H_EMPROR_C}Holy Roman Empire{##}.
The End Is Only the Beginning

A noble dynasty from the County of Luxembourg that rose to rule {H_BOH_C}Bohemia{##}, Hungary, and the {H_EMP_C}Empire{##} in the 14th and early 15th centuries, ending with {H_SIG_C}Sigismund's{##} death in 1437.
House of Luxembourg
Noble House

A {H_BOH_C}Bohemian{##} religious reform movement that rose in rebellion after the burning of {H_JANHUS_C}Jan Hus{##} at the {H_COUOFCON_C}Council of Constance{##} in 1415. They rejected {H_SIG_C}Sigismund's{##} claim to the Bohemian crown and successfully fought off five crusades over the next two decades, winning partial recognition of their faith in 1436.
Hussites
Religious Movement

{H_BOH_C}Bohemian{##} priest, scholar, and rector of the University of {H_PRA_C}Prague{##}. At the beginning of the 15th century, he became a popular preacher in Bohemia, known for delivering his sermons in Czech and condemning the wealth and corruption of the Catholic Church. Excommunicated in 1411, he was burned at the stake at the {H_COUOFCON_C}Council of Constance{##} in 1415 despite {H_SIG_C}King Sigismund's{##} promise of safe-conduct, sparking the {H_HUS_C}Hussite{##} revolt.
Jan Hus
c. 1360 – 11 October 1424

A one-eyed {H_BOH_C}Bohemian{##} nobleman and veteran of the {H_BATOFGRU_C}Battle of Grunwald{##} (1410) against the Teutonic Order. He rose to fame after the burning of {H_JANHUS_C}Jan Hus{##} as the foremost {H_HUS_C}Hussite{##} military leader, employing unorthodox tactics like the wagon fort (Wagenburg) and handgunners. He lost his second eye during the siege of {H_RAB_C}Rabí{##} in 1421, but, now fully blind, continued to defeat {H_SIG_C}King Sigismund's{##} armies. He died of the plague in 1424, undefeated in battle.
Jan Žižka

Margrave of Moravia and Brandenburg, elected {H_KINOFROM_C}King of the Romans{##} in 1410. Cousin of {H_SIG_C}Sigismund of Luxembourg{##}. Died in {H_BRN_C}Brno{##} under suspicious circumstances only three months after his election.
Jobst of Moravia

The title held by the elected ruler of the {H_EMP_C}Holy Roman Empire{##}. Not to be confused with the Emperor — a higher dignity requiring papal coronation in Rome, which many Kings of the Romans never received. The King was chosen by the seven {H_ELE_C}prince-electors{##} and held formal authority across the entire Empire, though in practice his power was strongest in the German lands and weakest in Bohemia and Italy.
King of the Romans

Word spreads like wildfire across the {H_EMP_C}Empire{##}: {H_JOBOFMOR_C}Jobst of Moravia{##}, the {H_KINOFROM_C}King of the Romans{##}, is dead. Mere months after his election to the crown. The official word speaks of illness, but this is an explanation too convenient for many. They whisper of poison, for his cousin and bitter rival {H_SIG_C}Sigismund{##} now stands without challenger, after being denied the throne at the last election.
The {H_ELE_C}electors{##} are gathering again, and there is little doubt whom they will choose this time.
The King is dead; long live the King!

Anger spreads across {H_BOH_C}Bohemia{##}: {H_JANHUS_C}Jan Hus{##}, lured to attend the {H_COUOFCON_C}Council of Constance{##} under {H_SIG_C}Sigismund's{##} promise of safe-conduct, has been tried and condemned by the Catholic Church. Offered his life if he recanted, he stayed faithful, even in the face of certain death.
The people of Bohemia, outraged by Sigismund's betrayal and the branding of their faith as heresy, are turning even further from Rome, and voices of rebellion grow louder every day.
Jan Hus Burned at the Stake

The faith wages war against itself. {H_WEN_C}King Wenceslaus{##}, pressured by his brother {H_SIG_C}King Sigismund{##} and the pope, ordered Catholic priests restored to {H_HUS_C}Hussite{##} parishes. In response, a great procession of Hussites stormed the New Town Hall in {H_PRA_C}Prague{##} and hurled the burgomaster and his Catholic councillors onto the spears of the crowd below. Tens of thousands are in uproar across the kingdom!

Now word comes that King Wenceslaus himself is dead, some even say the shock of the news struck him down. Sigismund alone stands to inherit the crown, but the Hussites have not forgotten his betrayal of {H_HUS_C}Jan Hus{##} to the flames and would rather see the kingdom burn than bow to him.
Bohemia in Flames

Following Pope Martin V's call for a crusade, {H_SIG_C}King Sigismund{##} marched into {H_BOH_C}Bohemia{##} at the head of a large crusader army, intent on taking his crown by force and driving out the {H_HUS_C}Hussites{##} once and for all.

At Vítkov Hill just outside {H_PRA_C}Prague{##}, his army met a small force of defending Bohemians. Peasants, townsfolk, and some say even women stood against the overwhelming force of the King. They were led by {H_JANZIZ_C}Jan Žižka{##}, a one-eyed Bohemian nobleman and veteran captain who once fought against the Teutonic Knights at the famous {H_BATOFGRU_C}battle of Grunwald{##}. Against all odds, the defenders successfully held against thousands of Sigismund's soldiers and broke the crusaders' assault.
This marks a turning point in the conflict between the Hussites and Sigismund, who, it seems, cannot win his crown by force alone.
Battle of Vítkov Hill

Two years after the Battle of Vítkov Hill, {H_JANZIZ_C}Jan Žižka{##} is a name spoken either in awe or in fear. He defeated {H_SIG_C}Sigismund{##} at {H_VYS_C}Vyšehrad{##} and even after losing his remaining eye to an arrow at {H_RAB_C}Rábí{##}, he still commands the {H_HUS_C}Hussites{##} of {H_BOH_C}Bohemia{##}.

Said to be guided by the voice of God himself, Žižka remains undefeated. Earlier this year, he destroyed a second crusader army at {H_NEM_C}Německý Brod{##}, not far from {H_KUT_C}Kuttenberg!{##} King Sigismund fled the field and his men drowned by the hundreds while crossing the frozen river.
The second crusade is broken and the war has come to our very doorstep.
Žižka the Blind

{H_JANZIZ_C}Jan Žižka{##}, the hope of {H_BOH_C}Bohemia's{##}, is dead — killed not by the sword but by the plague, while besieging the Catholic town of {H_PRI_C}Přibyslav{##} in {H_MOR_C}Moravia{##}. His followers are devastated. They now call themselves the Orphans, declaring their father has died.
{H_PROTHEGRE_C}Prokop the Great{##} now leads the {H_HUS_C}Hussites{##}, but he is only a priest. Can he fill the role left by Žižka — or is this the end of their cause?
Death of a Legend
This is the final year of the demo, but {H_BOH_C}Bohemia's{##} turbulent history continues for many more years.

{H_JANZIZ_C}Žižka's{##} followers will continue the fight, but internal division will ultimately lead to the {H_BATOFLIP_C}end of the Hussite Wars{##} in 1434, and in 1436 the Catholic Church will accept some of the {H_HUS_C}Hussites'{##} religious practices.

King {H_SIG_C}Sigismund{##} will be crowned {H_EMPROR_C}Holy Roman Emperor{##} in 1433, only to die in 1437. His reign will be remembered as one of great ambition and bitter cost, condemned in {H_BOH_C}Bohemia{##} for the burning of {H_JANHUS_C}Jan Hus{##}, the very kingdom his father {H_CHA4_C}Charles IV{##} had made the heart of the {H_EMP_C}Empire{##}.
The final version of The Guild 1 Remake: Europa 1410 will carry you through all of these historic milestones, and many more, that will change how you experience the game.

Younger son of {H_CHA4_C}Emperor Charles IV{##} and brother of {H_WEN_C}King Wenceslaus IV{##} of {H_BOH_C}Bohemia{##}. King of Hungary from 1387, elected {H_KINOFROM_C}King of the Romans{##} in 1411 after the death of his rival {H_JOBOFMOR_C}Jobst of Moravia{##}, and finally crowned {H_EMPROR_C}Holy Roman Emperor{##} in Rome in 1433.

Sigismund was a multilingual and charismatic leader. He summoned the {H_COUOFCON_C}Council of Constance (1414–1418){##} to end the Western Schism that had divided the Church for forty years. He allowed the burning of {H_JANHUS_C}Jan Hus{##} at the same council despite his own promise of safe-conduct. The {H_HUS_C}Hussites{##} took this as an act of betrayal, and it cost him the Bohemian crown for more than two decades. Only in 1436, a year before his death, did the Hussites finally accept him as King of Bohemia, and only after the {H_COMOFBAS_C}Compacts of Basel{##} granted their faith partial recognition.

He died in {H_ZNO_C}Znojmo{##} in {H_MOR_C}Moravia{##} in 1437, leaving no male heir. With him the {H_HOUOFLUX_C}House of Luxembourg{##} ended its century on the Imperial throne; his crowns passed to his son-in-law Albert of Habsburg, beginning the Habsburg ascendancy that would shape Central Europe for the next five hundred years.
